# Original Advanced Audio Coding (AAC) test fixtures

Generated by Codex for Jack, October 19, 2026; MIT OR Apache-2.0.
No recorded audio or third-party samples. Input: one second at 48000 hertz, 16-bit signed
samples, amplitude 2000. Channel c is round(2000 * sin(2*pi*(220+c*110)*i/48000)).
Stereo uses two channels; surround uses six in waveform-file channel order.

he-v1.m4a: afconvert -f m4af -d aach -b 32000 stereo.wav he-v1.m4a
he-v2.m4a: afconvert -f m4af -d aacp -b 32000 stereo.wav he-v2.m4a
aac-51.m4a: afconvert -f m4af -d 'aac ' -b 256000 surround.wav aac-51.m4a
lc-stereo.m4a: ffmpeg -i stereo.wav -c:a aac -b:a 128k -f ipod lc-stereo.m4a
lc-stereo.aac: ffmpeg -i stereo.wav -c:a aac -b:a 128k -f adts lc-stereo.aac

Apple's encoder chooses 32000-hertz output for high-efficiency version 1 at this bitrate; version 2 is 48000.
FFmpeg 9.0.2 independently decodes the three Apple files and the LC container to exactly
one second. The ADTS elementary stream has no container gapless metadata; it has encoder
priming and padding and is therefore intentionally longer. Binary hashes are in the review
manifest. Regeneration requires the encoders; normal regression tests use these fixed files.
